A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same study, with complete main texts and appendices. Corresponding equations, experiments, figures, and tables can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training, activation-patching, probing, generalization, attention, and curriculum experiments on permutation tracking, including additional results in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds probing and patching variability analyses and experiments with natural-language permutation instructions.

M1.justification: The candidate algorithms, AA/PAA mechanism sketches, symbolic-task training loss, and mechanism-steering curricula are retained. The natural-language experiment applies the existing interpretability framework without introducing a new proposed algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: v3 Appendix E adds an S3 task expressed through natural-language swap and rotation instructions, extending the atomic-permutation inputs to multi-token instructions. This is a limited input-domain extension of the same permutation problem; the original S3/S5 and curriculum coverage remains.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the GPT-2/Pythia comparisons, pretrained/from-scratch conditions, and pretraining controls and curricula. The added language experiment uses existing Pythia initialization conditions and introduces no new baseline method.

E3.justification: The added language experiment predicts and probes the final state at the final period token and patches prefixes at fixed token positions despite unequal action lengths. The original symbolic protocol retains one million length-100 sequences per group, the 90/10 split, and the stated training settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds checks of patching-signature consistency across input pairs in Appendix B and probe sensitivity to training subsets and training randomness in Appendix C.1. Existing deletion-patching, representation, attention, model-size, and curriculum analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 already reports data-order seeds, parity-head standard deviations, and confidence-based attention comparisons. v3 additionally reports patching standard deviations across 200 S3 input pairs and probe-accuracy standard deviations across ten probes trained on ten random subsets per model/probe type. This expands uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in main-model training runs.

E6.justification: The matched synthetic-task results are retained, including identical parity-head entries in v1 Table 1 and v3 Table 2. New results include S3 probe standard deviations below 10^-3, patching-variability maps, and language-task signatures consistent with PAA for pretrained Pythia and an associative mechanism for the scratch model (v3 Figure 14). These are additional findings under new analyses or conditions.

T1.justification: The formal permutation definitions, algorithm recurrences, Appendix A constant-depth argument, and parity-head definition are unchanged. The added discussion of long-input limitations in Section 2.1 supplies cited background without changing the formal analysis.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a limited claim of preliminary evidence for the mechanisms on language-expressed permutation tasks. The central two-mechanism and steering claims remain. Better AA generalization and faster convergence become explicit in the abstract but were already claimed in v1's conclusion.

C2.justification: New Appendix E tentatively attributes earlier computation in pretrained models to language understanding or pretrained tracking abilities. It also qualifies the scratch model's exact AA identification and acknowledges that unequal action-token lengths complicate patching alignment. These add substantive interpretations and limitations for the new setting.

D1.justification: Appendix E documents instruction-to-permutation examples, the final-period readout location, and differing token lengths for swap and rotation actions. Original optimizer settings, topic-model parameters, and code/data access information are retained; moving the repository link into the abstract does not change availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds Nanda et al. (2023) on decodable representations and several references supporting the discussion of transformer state-tracking limits in Section 2.1. The positioning relative to associative scans and heuristic mechanisms remains. Publication and bibliographic updates to existing references do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: v3 corrects typos and repeated words, tightens passages in the abstract and main text, and adds subsection organization within the probing appendix. The main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable, with localized expansion for the added analyses.

P2.justification: v3 adds variability and language-experiment figures and a probe-standard-deviation table. Figure 1 gains a legend and explanatory annotations, some representation axes are relabeled, and v1 Figure 14 moves from the appendix to main-text Figure 6. Most existing graphical content is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the evidence by quantifying variability in the central interpretability signatures and testing related mechanisms with language instructions (Appendices B, C, and E). Clearer presentation also helps. The extension remains narrow, with acknowledged token-alignment and mechanism-identification limitations, so these additions support a limited overall improvement.
